title: `FileAccess.get_open_error` squashes errors returned by `stat` call
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible on Arch Linux, Godot v4.6.2.stable.mono (001aa128b)

### System information

Godot v4.6.2.stable.mono (001aa128b) - Arch Linux #1 ZEN SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri, 01 May 2026 16:30:13 +0000 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti (nvidia; 595.71.05) - AMD Ryzen 7 5700X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 78.44 GiB memory

### Issue description

After calling `FileAccess.open` on a file that fails to stat (due to permissions, or any other error stat can run into), `FileAccess.get_open_error` will return a generic `ERR_FILE_CANT_OPEN` instead of the underlying error. This is particularly notable if one tries to write a file in a directory they don't have permissions for. 

While not a concern for most games, it is a concern for those developing applications using Godot and GDScript. since it prevents informing the user as to why a file operation failed. 

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/720caf476d0d2b322177b5f69916fd20be2f9e0b/drivers/unix/file_access_unix.cpp#L92-L100

The above piece of code seems to be primarily responsible for squashing `stat` errors into `ERR_FILE_CANT_OPEN`

It also seems to flow into other parts of the engine like GLTFDocument.write_to_filesystem, which also can't return accurate errors, instead returning a generic `FAILED` code.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a file owned by root in your home directory:
`sudo touch ~/test_file`

Running Godot as your normal user, run the following:
```gdscript
var file := FileAccess.open("~/file_you_cant_write", FileAccess.WRITE)
var err := FileAccess.get_open_error()
assert(err == Error.ERR_FILE_NO_PERMISSION, "Error returned from open() incorrect")
```

You should trigger the assert
